notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Tyler Bertuzzi is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Patrick Kane is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Teuvo Teräväinen has taken his spot beside Frank Nazar and Oliver Moore.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 19 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Ian Cole has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 33% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 79:38 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Wyatt Kaiser is suspended and has missed the last 3 games. Ian Cole has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov.
Luke Glendening joined from NYR on Nov 23 and has played beside Jordan Greenway and Cole Smith.
They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Dawson Mercer takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4.

Dylan DeMelo is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. Henry Thrun has taken his spot beside Mario Ferraro. That pair has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:14 together, up from 51% with DeMelo.

Isak Rosén is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. Viggo Björck has taken his spot beside Adam Lowry and Alex Iafallo. That line has had 81% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:18 together, up from 49% with Rosén.
Henry Thrun was added to the roster on Nov 14 and has played beside Mario Ferraro.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.

story.head: The Blackhawks are on a heater
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Jets have won three straight, and the Blackhawks have won four straight. The Blackhawks played last night, and the Jets are rested. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Blackhawks last (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Jets fifth (tied for ninth). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Blackhawks’ record (.423) is about what their chances are worth. The Jets’ record (.593) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.524), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Blackhawks (2nd) and the Jets (3rd) both get their shots through to the net. The Hawks don’t block many shots (31st). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so the Jets have the edge over them on the power play. Chicago has allowed 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Jets, they create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd) and keep things calm after the whistle (4th lowest).

Roman Kantserov (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 26 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Sam Rinzel (2 G / 16 A / 18 P in 25 GP) is next in line. Kyle Connor (22 G / 16 A / 38 P in 27 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is fifth in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (9 G / 25 A / 34 P in 27 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games.
Drew Commesso (1-0-0 / .880 SV% in 1 GS) will likely start for Chicago, and Stuart Skinner (9-5-4 / .892 SV% in 19 GS) for Winnipeg.
